who: Translates novels from Japanese and is slowly repairing an old wooden house in the mountains.

moments.plot: Proofs of the ferry novel are due, and the snow comes early this year.

tasks.title: Proofs, chapters 12 to 15
tasks.notes: Read the dialogue aloud. The captain never says please.

tasks.title: Nine words for drizzle
tasks.notes: The author has nine and English has three. Keep two, describe the rest.

tasks.title: Hana’s question about the last line
tasks.notes: She wants it longer. I want it shorter. The author is not answering.

tasks.title: Order wood before the road closes
Count the cracked tiles with Kenji

capture.title: Ask Kenji about the attic beam

file.title: Is there a word for ferry smell?
file.notes: Diesel, rope, oranges. Chapter 4 needs it in one line.

dated.title: Return the proofs
dated.notes: Scan them on {weekday+4} at the post office. The machine is slow before ten.

repeating.title: Walk round the roof
repeating.notes: Look for new gaps after the wind. Kenji has the long ladder.

attachments.notes: Six boats, two with the same name on purpose. Hana made a list. The harbour photo shows how they were painted.

agent.title: Find where the captain changes tone
agent.notes: I think I made him politer from chapter 9. List the lines so I can check.
agent.question: How much should I show you?
bodies: Seven lines from chapter 9 on are politer than before. Four say “please”, two say “would you”, and one apologises to a dog.
Seven lines from chapter 9 on are politer than before. Each one is below with the page that leads to it. The dog scene starts it.
agent.otherBody: Seven lines from chapter 9 on are politer than before. Your direction: {answer}
agent.otherAnswer: The lines and my old version
agent.acceptance: You know which lines to change.

discuss.title: Answer Hana about the last line
discuss.notes: Mine has six words. Hers has fourteen and explains the bell.
discuss.question: What would you defend?
bodies: Dear Hana, I would like to keep the six words. The bell has rung in every chapter, and I think the reader hears it without us.
Dear Hana, could we keep the bell but not explain it? Here is a version with nine words. I can live with nine.
discuss.otherBody: Dear Hana, about the last line: {answer}
discuss.otherAnswer: Keep the rhythm, lose a word
discuss.handoff: Your next step: send it to Hana
discuss.acceptance: Hana has an answer about the last line.

review.title: Find where the captain changes tone
review.note: Seven lines. The one with the dog may be on purpose.

review.title: Compare two gutter offers
review.note: Copper costs twice as much. Only one offer says how long it lasts.
